title: Cost-effective smartphone-based method for low range chemical oxygen demand analysis
author: Barbosa Segundo, Cardozo, et al.
materials: Kit of COD tube tests by HANNA (low range, 0 – 150 mg L−1, Reference n. HI93754F-25)
Potassium hydrogen phthalate of analytical grade

It was proved in previous work [1] that the present method achieve 97% of average accuracy, demonstrating that no significant statistical differences were attained when compared to the results from the spectrophotometer. The research was performed for the first time for COD analysis with the raw effluent samples and also synthetic ones, and also by treating electrochemically them, making sure that real water matrices with substantial organic load and salts content can be analyzed by this innovative protocol [14].

steps.title: Prepare 500 mg L⁻¹ KHP stock
steps.instruction: Weigh 250 mg of potassium hydrogen phthalate (KHP) and dissolve it in distilled water, making the final volume 500 mL to obtain a 500 mg L⁻¹ KHP stock solution (theoretical relationship: 1 mg KHP = 1.171 mg COD).

steps.title: Make calibration standards from stock
steps.instruction: Using the 500 mg L⁻¹ stock, pipette the volumes listed in Table 1 into the indicated volumetric flasks, fill to the mark with distilled water, and prepare at least duplicate vials for each standard (50 mL per vial is recommended for easy handling).

substeps.instruction: 125 mL → 120 mg L⁻¹ KHP → theoretical COD 140.5 mg O₂ L⁻¹
10.55 mL → 105 mg L⁻¹ KHP → theoretical COD 123.09 mg O₂ L⁻¹
90 mL → 105 mg L⁻¹ KHP → theoretical COD 87.86 mg O₂ L⁻¹
60 mL → 70.34 mg L⁻¹ KHP → theoretical COD 55.47 mg O₂ L⁻¹
45 mL → 55.47 mg L⁻¹ KHP → theoretical COD 52.73 mg O₂ L⁻¹
30 mL → 35.11 mg L⁻¹ KHP → theoretical COD 35.11 mg O₂ L⁻¹
15 mL → 17.6 mg L⁻¹ KHP → theoretical COD 17.6 mg O₂ L⁻¹
Distilled water → 0 mg L⁻¹ KHP → theoretical COD 0 mg O₂ L⁻¹

steps.title: Digest standards in HANNA COD tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer 2 mL of each prepared standard into a HANNA COD tube (range 0–150 mg L⁻¹ COD), digest at 150 °C for 2 h, then allow the tubes to cool to ambient temperature. If a sample’s expected COD exceeds 150 mg O₂ L⁻¹, dilute it before this step.

steps.title: Prepare vials and camera for imaging
steps.instruction: After cooling, thoroughly clean each glass vial to remove fingerprints or any residue; also clean the smartphone camera lens (both inside and outside) before each measurement.

steps.title: Set up standardized imaging conditions
steps.instruction: Place each vial on a white background, illuminate it with a constant artificial light source, and position the vial 2 cm from the background and at least 5 cm from the smartphone camera. Use a ruler to verify these distances for every sample.

steps.title: Capture saturation values with Color Grab
steps.instruction: Open the Color Grab app (Android), focus the camera on the vial so that the yellow circle appears, wait for the validation signal, then tap the screen to record the HSV values; note the saturation (S) value. Repeat this capture for all standards and samples, recording each saturation value.

steps.title: Construct calibration curve and calculate COD
steps.instruction: Plot the recorded saturation values against the theoretical COD values for the standards (using duplicates or triplicates), perform linear regression, and verify that the correlation coefficient (R²) exceeds 0.99. Use the resulting equation to compute COD concentrations of unknown samples.

description: This method is based on developing a calibration curve of potassium hydrogen phthalate standard solutions through using a smartphone camera with a specific app that transform the images of the samples in HSV (hue, saturation, value) values. In fact, the saturation (S) of the captured image shows a linear behavior that can be plotted and used for COD quantification because it represents the color intensity and its purity degree through the radial coordinate. This procedure permits to determine the COD results without the necessity of spectrophotometers, which have high associated costs for their adquisition and maintenance.
